concern_details.detail: What are the main components involved in the seat booking functionality?
concern_details.why: The packages match the booking path in the code. ReservationController and the Swing screens call LibraryFacade.makeReservation (LibraryFacade.java:117-118), which calls ReservationManager.makeReservation. That method resolves the student, room, area and slot through the registries, calls validateSeatInArea, validateUniqueness (Student), availableSeats (Area.getAvailableSeats) and selectSeat (the strategy), then createAndSave (ReservationRegistry) and notifyReservation (Observer to NotificationManager). The booking DTOs that the first critique asked for are now included.

concern_details.detail: What is each of these components responsible for?
concern_details.why: Each package has a one-line responsibility note, and the notes agree with the code. The Reservation manager note gives the makeReservation steps in the right order. The model note names the real rule predicates: Seat.isAvailable, Area.getAvailableSeats, Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot and StudyRoom.isOpenOnDate. The Registries note names ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot, which Seat.java:47 and StudyRoomManager.java:172 both use. Small inaccuracy: the model note groups StudyRoom.isOpenOnDate with the other predicates, but ReservationManager.resolveRoom is where it is enforced, together with room.isActive. That check is not mentioned.

concern_details.detail: How do these components interact with each other?
concern_details.why: The labelled dependencies match the code. NotificationScheduler calls facade.manageReservationEnd and sendReminders. FirstAvailableAssignment uses Seat. Seat, Area and Student call ReservationRegistry and StudyRoomRegistry ('checks occupancy'). NotificationManager updates through ReservationRegistry (NotificationManager.java:82). StudyRoomManager uses Seat.isAvailable and Area.getAvailableSeats (lines 289 and 381). One interaction is only implied: resMgr to notifMgr is an Observer attach/notify on Reservation (ReservationManager.notifyReservation), not a direct call. The label 'notifies' is acceptable at this level.

concern_details.detail: Which parts of the system may be affected by modifying the seat booking functionality?
concern_details.why: Each package has an 'Impact:' line with a reason, and Room availability manager is correctly flagged because it uses the same predicates. The view leaves out the existing tests, which the developer will have to update or extend: src/test/.../MakeReservationTest, AvailableStudyRoomsQueryTest, CancelReservationTest and PerformCheckInTest. The scheduler note says 'none for a booking rule'. Through the facade, the scheduler drives ReservationManager.manageReservationEnd and the reservation states, so a rule about booking lifetime (end, no-show, check-in window) would affect it. 'Unlikely' is more accurate than 'none'.

level_why: Thirteen packages in four groups, with one short note each and no classes, fits the balanced level. One cut is possible: the 'Booking data' group wraps a single package (Booking DTOs), so the wrapper can be dropped. Adding a test package would not take the view past the balanced level.
missing: The booking tests (src/test/java/it/unina/reservations/controller/MakeReservationTest, AvailableStudyRoomsQueryTest, CancelReservationTest, PerformCheckInTest) are part of what a rule change affects and should appear as one 'Booking tests' package that depends on the Library facade or the Reservation manager.

The room-level checks in ReservationManager.resolveRoom (room.isActive, room.isOpenOnDate) are where the existing date and room rules are enforced. The Reservation manager note should mention them next to 'validate seat'.
uml: Library facade, Reservation manager, Reservation scheduler and Notification manager are each one or two classes drawn as packages. This is a known compromise that the README explains, so it is acceptable, but marking them as classes nested in a 'controller' or 'boundary' package would be stricter UML for a package diagram.
The notes are not anchored to any element; they are only placed inside each package. Attaching each note to its package would make the reference explicit in UML terms.
fixes: Add a 'Booking tests' package (MakeReservationTest, AvailableStudyRoomsQueryTest, CancelReservationTest, PerformCheckInTest) with a dependency to the facade or the Reservation manager, and give it the impact note 'extend for the new rule'.
Change the Reservation scheduler impact note from 'none' to 'unlikely, unless the rule concerns reservation end, check-in or reminders' (it drives manageReservationEnd).
Mention the room checks (active, open on date) in the Reservation manager note, where resolveRoom enforces them.
Drop the single-child 'Booking data' wrapper and keep Booking DTOs as a top-level package.
